The zip corroborates precisely: his wife's firm's team page states that 'Malek resides in Lakeway with his wife, Fayruz Benyousef, and their daughter, Yara,' and Lakeway is 78738, the zip on this record. The federal data independently supports the household without contradicting anything: fec_donation_count of 0 is accurate — Malek has no federal record of his own — but a nationwide FEC search for 'Benyousef' returns exactly 5 results, all of them Fayruz Benyousef at Austin 78738-1802, giving to Doggett for Congress ($1,000 in both 2020 and 2022), ActBlue, Eddie for Texas and Sarver for Texas, a Democratic household pattern consistent with a $400 gift to Kirk Watson. He is now co-founder/co-owner of Austin Sol FC and serves as Vice President of Mentorship for 100 Black Men of Austin. Confidence is high on identity — name, occupation, employer and zip all line up. The industry label is a taxonomy judgment rather than a research gap: the list has no sports category, and Round Rock SC is a community youth club (U4-U19 recreational soccer with no tryouts, after-school programs run with local school districts) that also fields semi-pro sides, so Nonprofit / Advocacy fits it better than Entertainment — though note that RRSC's own site and its Givebutter donation page never state a 501(c)(3) status, and the separately registered Round Rock Soccer Association Inc (EIN 74-2035819, a 501(c)(3) amateur-sports org) cannot be confirmed as the same entity, since RRSC dates itself to 2017. One incidental note recorded for transparency but deliberately NOT entered as an affiliation: press coverage lists Shalom Austin, the Jewish federation organization, among the past clients of Fayruz Benyousef Consulting, the fundraising consultancy his wife founded and where he now works as office manager. That is a client relationship of his employer, not a personal membership, board seat or affiliation of his, and treating it as one would misrepresent him.

organizations.notes: Joe R. Long (b. Jan 13, 1930, San Antonio), Austin attorney-turned-banker and philanthropist, namesake of the Long Center for the Performing Arts ($20M lead gift with wife Teresa Lozano Long). Practiced administrative law 1965-1988 specializing in banking, savings & loan, insurance and securities regulation; co-organized First State Bank and Community National Bank and was Chairman & CEO of First State Bank 1989-1998 until its sale to Norwest (now Wells Fargo), consulting for Wells Fargo through Aug 2000; since then manages private investments. The filing's employer string 'Joe R. Long Investments' matches his own listed entity exactly and occupation 'investments' matches his post-banking role; the prolific federal giving record (222 donations) is consistent with a major Austin philanthropist. Deceased check: no obituary found; he was living and interviewed at his residence for a UT LLILAS-Benson piece published Oct 15, 2023, and the Long Center still lists him as living Chair Emeritus with no in-memoriam designation. The 2019 Sotheby's 'Collection of Joe R. & Teresa L. Long' sale was held while both were alive and is NOT an estate sale. His wife Teresa died Mar 21, 2021. The giving window (2022-04-12 to 2024-06-20) therefore does not post-date his death, though he would be 94 at the last gift and assisted/household giving cannot be fully excluded.
